items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I subbed in there a few times with Erskine Hawkins band

ctx.x: Yeah. Did you have occasion to play the Savoy?

The Savoy Ballroom, oh yeah, I played the Savoy Ballroom with Lucky Millinder, I played in there with Jimmy Lunceford’s band, I subbed in there a few times with Erskine Hawkins band, Jimmy Rushing had a band, I played with them a few times, I played a lot at the Savoy Ballroom. That was quite a place.
I just wish I could have been there. It sounds like a great scene.

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Erskine Hawkins and the Bama State Collegians – they would all – they would say, “Kid, you stick with it.”

ctx.x: I was going to say, that’s interesting. At the age of whatever it was, 13, you were playing with Duke Ellington.

Yeah. In a sense, yeah. And they were always – they were very encouraging. All those fellows – Count Basie’s band, Erskine Hawkins and the Bama State Collegians – they would all – they would say, “Kid, you stick with it.” And they remembered me when I finally became a professional player. They’d say, “I remember you from that children’s program.” And Louis, he remembered me. He’d say, “I remember you when you was a little boy.” He was great. He came to – I came to Witham Theater, and they introduced me to him. So…
But you had a different idea of what music was at that age. About how old were you when you were doing all of this, when you were playing on the kids’ show?
